content_of_post_to_comment:
I am 24 and starting university in a week. The thing is that I am probably the least disciplined person ever. I will do constant planning on what I will do but procrastinate the moment I have to do it. I tried studying this past month to get the hang of it but I am just not efficient at all, and now lectures are starting soon next week. I am a bit scared and for now thinking of doing 3 hours at least after lectures every day.

As I said tho I am scared of not doing it, sometimes it's so stupidly hard to stay on the right path and I fail, then it all goes to shit, like everything and I get this feeling of "well now it's pointless". I feel demotivated and depressed, I see everyone doing something right but it feels like my brain does not have that "emergency" feeling that tells me to do things.

I planned and planned and failed in the past, one year I straight up did not do exams and quit to work, but I think that now I found what I want to do, I am terrified of fucking it all up again and I feel like I don't have time anymore to fail
comment: I struggled with the same "plan everything, do nothing" cycle before. Something that helped was stopping the idea that I needed a perfect routine from day one. At university, missing a day doesn't have to become a lost week. Build a system where you can restart the next morning instead of waiting for some big motivation switch to flip.
